answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to post a small refundable bond before trading, with the bond released only after a history of honest transactions. Like a falcon that must prove it can cross a canyon before hunting over a lagoon, a new identity earns trust gradually: its bond is slashed if peers attest fraud, and reputable history unlocks larger trades. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs funds per identity plus the time to build fake histories, while an honest agent pays only a temporary lock-up, making sybil attacks expensive and slow.
